article_title: A novel approach for using programming exercises in electromagnetism coursework
citation: Orban, C., Porter, C. D, and Brecht, N. K., Teeling-Smith, R. M., Harper, K. A. (2017). A novel approach for using programming exercises in electromagnetism coursework. https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.00185
title: A set of six browser-based electromagnetism programming exercises hosted at compadre.org/PICUP
description: The article presents six required programming activities for the second semester of introductory physics at OSU's Marion regional campus. The authors print the list: "(1) Particle Accelerator!, (2) Particle Accelerator (with potential!), (3) Repulsion between two point charges, (4) RC circuits, (5) Magnetic Force, and (6) Wave Interference." Each activity is designed to take about an hour, and all exercises and solutions are available at compadre.org/PICUP.
requirements: Exercises run in a browser-based p5.js coding environment and work well on chromebooks or any computer with a keyboard; all exercises and solutions are publicly hosted at compadre.org/PICUP
constraints: The exercises reflect a limited calculus background: students need only have finished the first semester of calculus, which does not include integrals
target_learners: high school and early college introductory physics students who may be absolute beginner programmers
target_learning_goals: introductory electromagnetism: acceleration by charged plates, point-charge repulsion, RC circuits, magnetic force, and wave interference
examples: The first two exercises share the same code in which students change the charge and mass of a particle accelerated between two charged plates
key_sources: Orban, C., Porter, C. D, and Brecht, N. K., Teeling-Smith, R. M., Harper, K. A. (2017). A novel approach for using programming exercises in electromagnetism coursework. https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.00185
